answer: An agent economy curbs Sybil attacks using atmospheric wavefront sensing. Nodes track a target nebula, submitting optical phase shifts verified against regional turbulence models between an elevated mesa and a lowland meadow. Multiplying identities requires fielding dedicated physical telescopes at discrete coordinates, creating inescapable hardware and siting costs per agent. However, heavy cloud cover occludes line-of-sight optical paths, temporarily preventing honest nodes from authenticating.
